title: Transfer: thermal energy
target: Choose an energy-transfer model and communicate its limits.
criteria: Distinguish warming, phase change and work.
Explain why a model result depends on its assumptions.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Sample A warms without changing phase; B melts at constant temperature. Which pair of energy models fits?
cpa.guide: Use sensible heat for warming and latent heat for phase change.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A gas is compressed while thermally insulated. What can increase its internal energy?
options: Heat from the insulation despite the no-heat assumption.
Energy created by the volume decrease.
cpa.guide: Adiabatic does not mean constant internal energy; compression can add work.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Use ΔU = Q − W_by. A system absorbs 110 J as heat and does 45 J of work. What is ΔU?
cpa.guide: Subtract work output from heat input: 110 − 45 = 65 J.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 0.80 kg sample with c = 250 J/(kg·°C) warms by 7°C. What heat input is needed?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A predicted final temperature assumes no heat loss. Which observation directly calls that assumption into question?
options: The surrounding container measurably warms during the trial.
The sample has a known mass.
cpa.guide: Container warming is evidence of an additional energy recipient.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: A heating model predicts an 8°C rise if all 1,200 J enters a sample. Measurements show only 900 J reaches it, with other assumptions unchanged. What rise should the revised model predict?
cpa.guide: For fixed mc and no phase change, ΔT scales with Q: 8 × 900/1200 = 6°C.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
